source_family: the same five population trajectories used in the frozen Ecology Report
purpose: Search for simple quantitative regularities linking abundance decline to effective breeding-component contraction without reopening the frozen submission.

frozen_before_computation.candidate_rule_1: Within each population, fit log(E_t) = alpha + kappa * log(N_t). Report kappa and R2.
frozen_before_computation.candidate_rule_2: Fit a population-fixed-effect common elasticity using within-population demeaned log(E) and log(N). Report kappa_common and R2_within.
frozen_before_computation.candidate_rule_3: Fit separate fixed-effect elasticities for Palmer and Signy using the same within-population demeaning. Report kappa_Palmer and kappa_Signy.
frozen_before_computation.candidate_rule_4: For each population, at the first season with abundance <= 50%, 25%, and 10% of its first eligible-season abundance, report retained E as percent of first-season E. Thresholds that are never crossed remain missing.

secondary_descriptors: within-population Spearman correlation between abundance and E
abundance fraction at first season E falls to <=75% and <=50% of initial E, if reached
interpretation_rules: No p-value or threshold discovered here may alter the frozen Ecology Report.
A candidate 'sublinear contraction' rule requires all five annual log-log slopes to be >0 and <1; otherwise it is not called universal.
A common quarter-power or other named exponent will not be claimed unless confidence intervals from a future independent dataset support it; this exploration reports only the observed estimate.
Palmer versus Signy differences are descriptive because there are only two monitoring systems.
Threshold summaries are descriptive and not evidence for a causal tipping point.
